content.text: Flat neck veins; known hemorrhage; narrow pulse P; POCUS (flat IVC, flat ventricles)
Aggressive fluid resuscitation: saline, lactate ringer
blood products (1:1:1 ratio) for hemorrhagic shock
Low SpO2; cyanosis; airway compromise; look for airway obstruction, tension PTX, severe bronchospasm
Known DKA, sepsis, renal failure; widening QRS; ETCO2 very low
Sodium bicarbonate 1 mEq/kg IV for pH <7.1 or severe acidosis
Renal failure; dialysis; peaked T waves (hyperK); flat T/U waves (hypoK); ECG changes
HyperK: CaCl2 1 g (or Ca-gluconate) + bicarb + insulin-dextrose, can give albuterol
Cold environment; core temp <30°C; J (Osborne) waves; paradoxical undressing history
Active rewarming; defer extra meds until +30°C
Absent unilateral breath sounds; JVD; tracheal deviation; mechanism of trauma or mech vent; rapidly falling ETCO2 during CPR
Needle decompression: 14-16g needle at 2nd ICS MCL; OR B/L finger thoracostomies in arrest; follow w chest tube
JVD; Beck's triad; known malignancy, pericarditis, or trauma; POCUS (pericardial effusion wRA/RV collapse)
Drug ingestion history; empty pill bottles; specific toxidromes; EMS report; bradycardia or QRS widening
Naloxone (IN, IM, IV): opioid -give very slow IM or IV (projectile vomit)
Na bicarb for TCA/Na channel blockers
Sudden PEA arrest; known DVT/hypercoagulable; acute right heart strain on POCUS; S1Q3T3 ECG
Empiric alteplase 50 mg IV over 2 min if PE suspected or heparin drip
Chest pain preceding arrest; ST changes on monitor; post-ROSC STEMI
consider fibrinolysis in arrest only if PE distinguished from STEMI
